summary: Import-time dropper downloads and executes remote binary from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts
details: accounts-loading-state@8.9.6 executes a remote-payload dropper on require(). The package's index.js loads setup.js, which reconstructs download hostnames at runtime by joining split string fragments (e.g. ["oob-wor","ker.cf","99-9b3.wor","kers",".dev"].join("") yielding oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev, plus sibling hosts 100-416/101-adf/102-baf/103-070 and a DNS-TXT base64 fallback resolver at *.dl.well1.site). setup.js selects a platform-specific asset, downloads the binary via httpGet, writes it to a disguised cache path (e.g..cache/dotnet_diag), chmods it 0o755 on non-Windows, launches it detached, and unlinks the file after 5 seconds to remove on-disk traces. The advertised purpose ("accounts loading state adapter") is unrelated to fetching and executing native binaries; hostname obfuscation, disguised filenames, and post-execution cleanup indicate deliberate evasion. Fetching and executing attacker-controlled binaries on the installer host at import time is a supply-chain remote-code-execution vector.
